interest: This list of papers provides a valuable institutional window into how the U.S. Department of State tracked Japanese naval movements and naval diplomacy in the British Commonwealth during the interwar period. It documents visits by the Imperial Japanese Navy's Training Squadron—specifically the armored cruisers Asama and Yakumo—to major Australian ports, highlighting consular reporting on naval training cruises that carried sons of prominent Japanese officials. Furthermore, the cross-reference annotations to Australian general affairs (file 847.00) illuminate State Department recordkeeping practices and the intersection between naval surveillance and diplomatic observation in the Pacific.
keywords: Visits of Japanese Navy Vessels to Australia
overview: This file consists of a Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46) for classification 894.3347, concerning visits of Japanese naval vessels and aircraft to Australian ports between 1932 and 1935. The index catalogues three despatches sent by American consular officers in Sydney reporting on visits of the Japanese Naval Training Squadron, including the cruisers Asama and Yakumo calling at Fremantle, Adelaide, Melbourne, and Sydney, and notes cross-references to general Australian political records under file 847.00.

subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State Form DS-46 'List of Papers' dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing three consular despatches under the subject 'Visits of Japanese Navy Vessels to Australia'. It records a 1932 report from Sydney on a visit of the Japanese Naval Training Squadron, along with two 1935 cross-reference entries concerning training cruiser visits to Fremantle, Adelaide, Melbourne, and Sydney. The sheet notes that the 1935 reports regarding the cruisers Asama and Yakumo were filed under decimal file 847.00.
